title: A derived-complete module with finite residue over a complete Noetherian ring is finite
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal, and assume that the canonical map $A\to\widehat A=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/I^n$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $M$ be an $A$-module which is derived complete with respect to $I$, meaning that $M[0]$ is derived $I$-complete in $D(A)$ [def-weil-point-derived-complete-module-complex]. If $M/IM$ is a finitely generated $A/I$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], then $M$ is a finitely generated $A$-module. Moreover the canonical map $M\to\varprojlim_{n\geq1}M/I^nM$ is an isomorphism; this inverse limit consists of compatible sequences of residue classes, with componentwise operations.

source.place: Tag 09BA, lemma-derived-complete-finite, specialized to an I-adically complete ring A

proof.text: Products of modules are exact, verified by the forgetful functor to abelian groups. Apply [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence] to obtain countable products in D(A) preserved by every cohomology functor. For f in I, complete 1-s on the constant multiplication tower on M[0] to a Roos triangle [def-weil-derived-limit]. The first vertex is zero by [def-weil-point-derived-complete-module-complex], hence 1-s is an isomorphism by the distinguished-triangle zero-vertex criterion. Apply H^0, use H^0(M[0]) = M, and identify products of modules with sequences. Naturality identifies the resulting map with Delta_f(a)_n = a_n - f a_(n+1), so Delta_f is bijective. Only this direction of the criterion is needed.

For a linear map g:X -> M where Delta_f is bijective on X and M, Delta_f is bijective on range(g): injectivity follows from M; for surjectivity lift a range-valued sequence to X, solve there, and apply g. If N is a submodule of M and Delta_f is bijective on both N and M, it is bijective on M/N. Surjectivity follows by lifting a sequence and solving in M. For injectivity, lift a kernel sequence to x in the product of M. Delta_f(x) lies in the product of N; solve it there to obtain y. Then Delta_f(x-y)=0, so x=y and the quotient sequence is zero.

source.place: Tag 091U, cokernel closure via the sequence criterion

proof.text: For any ordinarily I-adically complete module N [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and f in I, Delta_f is bijective. The partial sums S(n,k)=sum_{j<k} f^j b_(n+j) are Cauchy since their tails belong to I^k N. Their limits a_n satisfy a_n-fa_(n+1)=b_n, using S(n,k+1)=b_n+f S(n+1,k) and separatedness. A kernel sequence satisfies a_n=f^k a_(n+k) for every k, so separatedness makes it zero.

Prove sequence Nakayama by induction on a finite set s of ideal generators. Assume Delta_f is bijective for every f in I and span(s) M=M. If s is empty then M=0. Otherwise choose f in s, put N=range(f:M -> M), and quotient by N. Step 2 gives the sequence conditions on M/N. The remaining generators span M/N because f acts as zero, so induction gives M/N=0. Thus multiplication by f on M is surjective. For m in M recursively choose preimages a_0=m and f a_(n+1)=a_n. Injectivity of Delta_f implies this sequence is zero, hence m=0.

Restrict the finite residue module from A/I to A using finiteness of A/I over A. Lift its finite generators to M and let N be their A-span [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Their images span M/IM, hence N+IM=M. The ring is ordinarily complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian] makes the finite module N complete. Step 3 gives its sequence conditions; steps 1 and 2 give those on M/N. The residue-generation equality gives I(M/N)=M/N. Choose a finite generating set of I by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and apply step 4. Thus M/N=0, N=M, and M is finite.

source.place: Tag 09BA, residue-generator construction, specialized to A complete

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian] once more to the now finite module M over the complete Noetherian ring A. The equivalence between ordinary completeness and bijectivity of AdicCompletion.of identifies its conclusion with the canonical compatible-residue map asserted in the statement.
